subject: Request: Temporary SLA waiver for new encoder beta launch
messages:
From: Ari Gold <ari@auroraai.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@auroraai.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Aurora launch — SLA question for encoder beta

Hi Soojin,

Quick one: Aurora plans to ship a new encoder-heavy ranking endpoint next month and we want to use Redwood's latest encoder (v0.9-beta) for cost/latency gains. Our legal/procurement team is asking for the usual 99.9% uptime + 100ms p95 latency for inference. Given this is a beta model you flagged as "preview", can Redwood provide a temporary SLA carve-out / waiver for the first 60 days? We'll accept an explicit degradation clause and a rollback trigger if latency consistently breaches a threshold.

Can you send the process or template we should expect? We need to close this as part of our launch checklist by 7/20.

Thanks,
Ari
VP Product, Aurora AI

Attachment: aurora_launch_plan_v2.pdf (doc stub)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Ari Gold <ari@auroraai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora launch — SLA question for encoder beta

Hi Ari — thanks for the heads up and congrats on the launch!

Short answer: we can do a time-limited SLA exception for a preview model, but we need a few items signed off first:
- A written temporary SLA waiver (60-day window) describing reduced commitments.
- A mutual action plan (MAP) that documents rollback/fallback models and escalation steps.
- A performance monitoring cadence (daily p95 and incident email) for the waiver period.

I'll loop in Marissa (sales ops) for contract language and Karthik for anything infra-related (quantization/ops risks). I'm happy to propose language and attach a draft waiver + the perf summary we ran internally.

Timelines: I can share a draft today and then we can iterate with Procurement.

- Soojin
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
(Attachment: rdw_temp_sla_waiver_draft.pdf)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Aurora launch — SLA question for encoder beta

Soojin / team — copying legal template language we typically use for temporary carve-outs. Key points to confirm with AurorA procurement:

1) Limited-scope waiver: Redwood will provide a documented waiver for model v0.9-beta covering uptime (reduced to 99.0%) and p95 latency (reduced to 200ms) for 60 calendar days starting on first production request.
2) Metrics & monitoring: Aurora will share an SLO dashboard access and Redwood will provide daily digest + immediate alert on sustained breach (>3 consecutive hours).
3) Rollback triggers: If p95 > 300ms for 24 hours or repeated incidents (3 incidents in 30 days), Redwood can force rollback to v0.8-stable and Aurora accepts temporary degraded results.
4) Liability: No change to indemnity, but credits for SLA misses limited to usage credits up to one month of committed capacity.

I'll attach the draft waiver in the thread. Keep the language tight — Procurement likes bullet points.

- Marissa
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: rdw_temp_sla_waiver_draft.pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Aurora launch — SLA question for encoder beta

Quick infra note from the ops side:
- v0.9-beta uses a new fused-kernel path that reduces cost but has narrow perf stability at extreme batch sizes. We validated p95 under our test workload at ~155ms but saw outliers when KV cache hits dropped below 40%.
- For production we recommend enforced fallback policy: route 90% of traffic to v0.9-beta, 10% to v0.8-stable for the first 2 weeks. That gives us a realtime safety net without full rollback.
- We'll enable extra tracing and keep a short retention window for traces during the waiver period.

I'll prepare an ops note to attach to the MAP.

— Karthik
Director, Serving Infrastructure
(Attachment: encoder_beta_perf_summary.pdf)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Ari Gold <ari@auroraai.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@auroraai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora launch — SLA question for encoder beta

Hi Ari — attaching the draft waiver + MAP and a short ops summary. Highlights:
- Temporary SLA: 60 days from first production request; uptime target 99.0%; p95 latency target 200ms.
- Fallback plan: automatic 10% traffic routing to v0.8-stable for first 14 days; rollback triggers spelled out.
- Credits: up to one month of committed reserved capacity for proven SLA misses.

If Procurement is good, sign the attached PDF and we'll countersign same day. If you prefer a 30-day trial instead of 60, we can do that but would prefer 60 to gather meaningful telemetry.

Next steps: Procurement to review + sign by 7/20 to meet your launch date.

Thanks,
Soojin
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(Attachments: rdw_temp_sla_waiver_draft.pdf; aurora_mutual_action_plan.docx)

From: Procurement Team <procurement@auroraai.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ari Gold <ari@auroraai.com>, Nora Patel <nora.patel@auroraai.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Aurora launch — SLA question for encoder beta

Thanks for the draft — procurement reviewed with legal. A few edits requested:
- Replace the 60-day auto-expiry with "60-day review with renewal option" language.
- Add clause for joint post-mortem within 48 hours of any rolling breach.
- Clarify monitoring access: request read-only dashboard token + daily CSV export.

We're otherwise good with the reduced uptime/p95 and the fallback traffic strategy. We're attaching a redline and will return the signed PDF if you accept the three small changes. Can Redwood confirm on the joint post-mortem and dashboard export?

Regards,
Procurement Team
Aurora AI
(Attachment: aurora_procurement_redline.pdf)
